title: Coprimality and gcd of a Finite Family of Totients $\{\varphi(n_i)\}_{i\in s}$
description: Answers the third open question of euler-totient-oq-07: generalize the two-argument coprimality characterization to a finite family {φ(n_i)}_{i∈s}. Call an argument non-unital when n ∉ {1,2} (equivalently φ(n) ≠ 1); every non-unital argument has 2 ∣ φ(n), unifying the n = 0 case (φ 0 = 0) with the n ≥ 3 case (Nat.totient_even). The headline `pairwise_coprime_totient_iff` shows the family is pairwise coprime iff at most one index is non-unital — two distinct non-unital arguments would share the factor 2, while at most one non-unital argument leaves every pair with a unital member whose totient 1 is coprime to everything. For the whole-family gcd: all-non-unital ⟹ 2 ∣ gcd, and nonempty with all arguments ≥ 3 ⟹ 2 ≤ gcd. The 'fixed power of 2' sub-question is settled by `family_gcd_isPowerOfTwo`: if every φ(n_i) is a power of 2 (as for products of distinct Fermat primes) then so is the family gcd, since a divisor of a prime power is a prime power. Fully machine-checked: 0 sorries, 0 axioms (the `decide` calls are kernel reductions over concrete small naturals, not `native_decide`).

mathlibDependencies.description: `(φ m).Coprime (φ n) ↔ (m = 1 ∨ m = 2) ∨ (n = 1 ∨ n = 2)`. The two-argument coprimality characterization, restated through `Unital` and lifted to the pairwise level.
`2 < n → Even n.totient`. Supplies 2 ∣ φ(n) for non-unital arguments with n ≥ 3, the engine behind both the pairwise characterization and the family gcd divisibility.
`φ n = 1 ↔ n = 1 ∨ n = 2`. Identifies the unital arguments with the totient-1 set, giving `totient_eq_one_iff_unital`.
`#s ≤ 1 ↔ ∀ a ∈ s, ∀ b ∈ s, a = b`. Encodes 'at most one non-unital index' as a cardinality bound on the filtered set in `pairwise_coprime_totient_iff`.

The Finset gcd API: 2 divides the family gcd iff it divides every member; the gcd divides any one member; the gcd is zero iff all members vanish. Drives the whole-family divisibility, lower bound, and power-of-two results.
`Prime p → (i ∣ p ^ m ↔ ∃ k ≤ m, i = p ^ k)`. With p = 2: a divisor of a power of 2 is a power of 2, giving `family_gcd_isPowerOfTwo` from the gcd dividing one power-of-two member.

originalContributions: `two_dvd_totient_of_not_unital`: `n ∉ {1,2} ⟹ 2 ∣ φ n`, unifying the n = 0 case (φ 0 = 0) with the n ≥ 3 case (`Nat.totient_even`) into a single 'non-unital ⟹ even totient' lemma — the basic obstruction at the family level.
`pairwise_coprime_totient_iff`: the headline finite-family characterization — {φ(n_i)}_{i∈s} is pairwise coprime iff the non-unital indices number at most one (`(s.filter (¬Unital ∘ n)).card ≤ 1`).
`two_dvd_family_gcd_of_forall_not_unital`: if every argument is non-unital then 2 divides the gcd of the whole family.
`two_le_family_gcd_of_forall_three_le`: a nonempty family with all arguments ≥ 3 has family gcd ≥ 2 — the quantitative floor, generalizing the parent's two-argument `2 ≤ gcd(φ m, φ n)`.
`family_gcd_isPowerOfTwo`: settles the 'fixed power of 2' sub-question — if every φ(n_i) is a power of 2 then so is the family gcd (a divisor of a prime power is a prime power).
prerequisites: Parity of φ: φ(n) is even for n > 2; φ(0) = 0, φ(1) = φ(2) = 1

relatedProblems.relationship: Parent: oq-07 characterizes coprimality of two totients and records 2 ≤ gcd(φ m, φ n) for m, n ≥ 3. This entry answers its third open question by lifting the picture to a finite family — pairwise coprimality, whole-family gcd divisibility, and the power-of-two case.
Sibling: oq-06 proves the parity classification φ(n) even ⟺ n ∉ {1, 2}. The 'non-unital ⟹ even totient' lemma here is the family-level use of that classification (extended to cover n = 0).

overview.historicalContext: Euler introduced φ(n), the order of (ℤ/nℤ)ˣ, in his 1763 generalization of Fermat's little theorem. The parent entry euler-totient-oq-07 settled when two totients are coprime: never, once both arguments exceed 2, because −1 has order 2 in the unit group and Lagrange forces 2 ∣ φ(k) for k > 2. The natural next question — posed as the third open question of oq-07 — is what happens for a whole finite family of arguments: when are the totients pairwise coprime, and what can be said about the gcd of the entire family? Both reduce to a single notion: an argument is 'non-unital' when it lies outside {1, 2}, equivalently when φ ≠ 1, and every non-unital argument contributes the factor 2.
overview.problemStatement: **Open Question (euler-totient-oq-07-oq-03):** generalize the two-totient coprimality characterization to a finite family {φ(n_i)}_{i∈s}: when is the family pairwise coprime, and when is the gcd of the whole family a fixed power of 2?
overview.text: The family {φ(n_i)}_{i∈s} is pairwise coprime iff at most one index is non-unital (n_i ∉ {1,2}). If every argument is non-unital the family gcd is even, and for arguments ≥ 3 it is at least 2. If every φ(n_i) is a power of 2 then the family gcd is a power of 2.
overview.proofStrategy: Everything funnels through the predicate `Unital n := n = 1 ∨ n = 2` and the lemma `two_dvd_totient_of_not_unital` (n ∉ {1,2} ⟹ 2 ∣ φ n, splitting on n = 0 vs n ≥ 3). The pairwise characterization rewrites `Finset.card_le_one` and uses the two-argument iff `coprime_totient_iff_unital` in both directions: distinct non-unital indices break coprimality, while a unital member in every pair restores it. The whole-family gcd results apply `Finset.dvd_gcd` (2 divides every member ⟹ divides the gcd), `Finset.gcd_eq_zero_iff` (positivity of the gcd from a positive member), and `Nat.dvd_prime_pow` (the gcd divides a power-of-two member, hence is itself a power of 2). Worked examples evaluate φ and gcd at concrete tuples — (1,2,9), (9,15), (5,7,9), and the Fermat primes (3,5,17) — by kernel `decide`.
keyInsights: **One notion controls everything: non-unitality.** An argument is non-unital (n ∉ {1,2}) exactly when φ(n) ≠ 1, and exactly then 2 ∣ φ(n). Pairwise coprimality and family-gcd parity both reduce to counting non-unital indices.

**Pairwise coprime ⟺ at most one non-unital argument.** Coprimality is a property of pairs; the only obstruction is two non-unital arguments sharing the factor 2, so the whole family is pairwise coprime precisely when the non-unital indices number ≤ 1.
**The n = 0 boundary merges with n ≥ 3.** φ(0) = 0 is even, so the clean statement is in terms of {1, 2} (the φ = 1 set), not in terms of a size threshold — covering 0 and all of n ≥ 3 uniformly.

**The power-of-2 question is a divisor-of-prime-power fact.** Once every φ(n_i) is a power of 2, the family gcd divides one of them and is therefore a power of 2 — no further arithmetic of the n_i is needed. This holds for products of distinct Fermat primes, where φ is always a power of 2.
prerequisites: Euler's totient φ and the unit group (ℤ/nℤ)ˣ
Parity of the totient and the value φ = 1 at exactly {1, 2}
Divisors of prime powers; finite evaluation by kernel `decide`

conclusion.summary: For a finite family {φ(n_i)}_{i∈s}: it is pairwise coprime iff at most one argument lies outside {1, 2}; if all arguments are non-unital the family gcd is even; for arguments ≥ 3 (nonempty) the gcd is at least 2; and if every φ(n_i) is a power of 2 then so is the family gcd. 7 theorems, 1 definition, 185 lines, 0 sorries, 0 axioms; built on Mathlib's `Nat.totient_coprime_totient_iff`, `Nat.totient_even`, the Finset gcd API, and `Nat.dvd_prime_pow`.
conclusion.implications: The pairwise characterization is the practical form: a collection of totients can be pairwise coprime only if all but one argument are 1 or 2, so any construction needing many pairwise-coprime totients is essentially impossible. The power-of-2 result pinpoints exactly when the family gcd stays 2-smooth — when each φ(n_i) is a power of 2 — connecting to products of distinct Fermat primes, the classical 2-power-totient numbers.
openQuestions: Compute the exact value of the family gcd in terms of the factorizations of the n_i via φ(n) = ∏ p^(k−1)(p−1) — e.g. the largest odd common factor.
Characterize precisely which n have φ(n) a power of 2 (constructible-polygon / Fermat-prime numbers) and feed that back into `family_gcd_isPowerOfTwo`.
Study the dual extremal question: the maximal size of a set of arguments whose totients are pairwise coprime within a bounded range, and its growth rate.

sections.title: Module Overview, the Unital Predicate, and the Even-Totient Lemma
sections.summary: Module docstring framing the finite-family open question, imports (`Mathlib`), and namespace opening `Nat`/`Finset`. Defines `Unital n := n = 1 ∨ n = 2` with its `DecidablePred` instance, proves `totient_eq_one_iff_unital` (φ n = 1 ↔ Unital n), the key `two_dvd_totient_of_not_unital` (non-unital ⟹ 2 ∣ φ n, via case split on n = 0 vs n ≥ 3), and `coprime_totient_iff_unital` (the two-argument iff restated through Unital).

sections.title: Pairwise Coprimality of the Family
sections.summary: `pairwise_coprime_totient_iff`: the family {φ(n_i)}_{i∈s} is pairwise coprime iff the filtered set of non-unital indices has cardinality ≤ 1. Forward direction derives a contradiction from two distinct non-unital indices (shared factor 2); backward direction shows any pair must contain a unital member, hence coprime, using `Finset.card_le_one` and `coprime_totient_iff_unital`.

sections.title: gcd of the Whole Family
sections.summary: `two_dvd_family_gcd_of_forall_not_unital` (all non-unital ⟹ 2 ∣ family gcd via `Finset.dvd_gcd`), `two_le_family_gcd_of_forall_three_le` (nonempty, all ≥ 3 ⟹ 2 ≤ gcd, using `Finset.gcd_eq_zero_iff` for positivity), and `family_gcd_isPowerOfTwo` (all φ(n_i) powers of 2 ⟹ family gcd is a power of 2, via `Finset.gcd_dvd` and `Nat.dvd_prime_pow`).

sections.title: Worked Examples
sections.summary: Concrete tuples: (1,2,9) pairwise coprime (one non-unital index); (9,15) not pairwise coprime (two non-unital indices sharing 2); (5,7,9) with family gcd ≥ 2; and the Fermat primes (3,5,17) with φ = (2,4,16), all powers of 2, so the family gcd is a power of 2.
